graph.title: LEGO Architecture 21032 Sydney
notes: The booklet is one model (Sydney skyline: base, Harbour Bridge, Deutsche Bank Place, Sydney Tower, Opera House). Total nodes = 361: 277 explicit parts (b1-b277) plus repeats (pylon 4x8, mod 4x7, sailA 2x3, sailB 2x4, sailC 2x5).

Exact stud-to-stud mappings are not legible in the isometric drawings, so most joined edges use null ports and connect each new piece to the piece(s) it sits on; some placements (which base plate carries which sub-assembly, which jumper plate carries which piece) are best-guess.

Part identification from images and element-count matching: step 6/19 side-stud 2x2 plates = lego-99206; steps 7/12/22 = lego-87609; the bridge 'handle' plates (60478) clip into the clip tiles (15712) and the 3L/4L bars stand on jumper studs; bridge arch segments are chained by clip (63868) on handle (60478) bars.

Deutsche Bank Place modules (steps 58, 60 x2, 62) are the 'mod' repeat; mod1..mod4 stack bottom-to-top with the plate layers b156-b158 and b159-b161 between them; the four clips per module are c1/c2 (left side) and c3/c4 (right side). Which bar sits in which clips is inferred.
Tower base block (steps 78-84) is treated as a sub-assembly placed on the 76/77 block in step 85; the Sydney Tower shaft is joined with axle/axle-hole and pin links in steps 86-95.
Opera House sails are hinged on 3937 hinge bases; which sail group sits on which hinge base (sailA on b268/b269, sailB on b270/b271, sailC on b263/b264) is assumed.
